tone_benchmark: supplied Physics textbook / Conceptual Physics-style student prose, adapted to college-level AP Calculus precision
principles: Use direct, concrete high-school prose while preserving AP-level mathematical precision and conditions.
Introduce the mathematical idea or representation before burying students in notation; then use notation accurately and consistently.
Keep explanatory paragraphs short enough for annotation and discussion. Notes reading passages normally use several short paragraphs rather than one dense block.
Treat graphs, tables, formulas, and diagrams as evidence. Ask what they show and how representations agree before treating them as decoration.
Explain what a derivative, integral, limit, or differential equation means before reducing it to a procedure when the section is conceptual or contextual.
Use theorem names only with their conditions/hypotheses; avoid slogan-level theorem use.
In context, name variables and units naturally. Do not add fake real-world nouns merely to make a routine symbolic problem look contextual.
Respect student intelligence: accessible does not mean childish, chatty, or vague.

notes_reading.default: 3–5 short paragraphs, usually 2–4 sentences each when explanatory reading is needed

avoid: generic “justify your answer” tails where no specific justification target exists
repeated Student A/Student B shell across unrelated families
